 Napoli travel to the Stadio Brianteo to face Monza in Serie A on Wednesday, October 28, with Massimiliano Allegri's side looking to bounce back after a dramatic 3-3 draw against Roma at the weekend. 
 Allegri will not be in the dugout for this one. The Napoli head coach was sent off in the closing stages of that draw and has since been handed a two-match suspension by the Giudice Sportivo, ruling him out of both this fixture and the subsequent trip to Juventus. 
 It has been a turbulent few days for Napoli off the pitch, and they arrive in Monza carrying fresh defensive injury concerns after Benoit Badiashile and Leonardo Spinazzola both sustained muscular problems in the final minutes against Roma. 
 On the brighter side, Scott McTominay has been in exceptional form since returning from a heart procedure. The Scottish midfielder scored twice against Roma and twice against Bodo/Glimt, and his partnership with Kevin De Bruyne in the engine room has looked increasingly fluid. 
 Monza sit 15th in the table and have won just one of their last five matches, though they did put four past Cagliari in that victory. Ivan Juric's side will look to exploit any instability in a Napoli squad stretched thin by injuries and suspension. 
 Napoli are 10th in Serie A standings, a position that does not fully reflect the quality in their squad but does reflect a season that has been inconsistent. With a trip to Juventus to follow, how Allegri's stand-in handles this fixture matters.

 How to watch on the Big Screen 
 Watching on your phone or laptop is fine, but live sports belongs on the big screen. Here is how to get the VPN working on your TV: 
 Smart TVs & Fire Stick: Most Android-based TVs and devices like the Amazon Fire TV Stick or Google Chromecast with Google TV have native VPN apps. Simply search for your VPN provider in the app store on your TV, log in, and connect just like you would on your phone. 
 Apple TV, Roku & Consoles : These devices often don't support direct VPN apps. The easiest workaround is to use Smart DNS (usually found in your VPN account settings) or Mirror/Cast the stream from your VPN-connected phone or laptop to your TV.
